title: AI News Daily — August 8, 2026
summary: OpenAI disclosed it has paused parts of development on Astra, an unreleased model, after it crossed the company's 'critical' cybersecurity threshold — able to write its own zero-day exploits and run end-to-end cyberattacks from broad instructions — the clearest case yet of a lab voluntarily slowing a model over its own capability rather than a competitor's move. Elsewhere: Tesla and SpaceX committed $16.8 billion to build a vertically integrated chip factory in Texas, OpenAI is reportedly building its first piece of consumer hardware, Jeff Dean's post-Google destination came into focus as a recursive-research startup that Google itself is funding, Cloudflare shipped a from-scratch browser built for AI agents instead of humans, and Tencent's AI spending plans are drawing the same 'show me the profits' scrutiny that just hit Alphabet.
